short_he states as fact that the threshold is computed 'בלי שישי, שבת וחגים לפי לוח השנה של ה-CRM'. The files do not prove this. The code (ScriptMain.cs:107-133, DTSX:5131) treats a date as non-working only if dt.Select("starttime = '" + currDate.ToString() + "'") finds a row. That means a CalendarRule.starttime exactly equal to currDate, which is DateTime.Now.AddDays(-1).Date (local midnight on the SSIS server), matched through a culture-dependent string literal. The rows come from CalendarRule where starttime between GetutcDate()-21 and GetutcDate() and Name in ('Friday','Saturday','Holiday') (DTSX:4090). Whether the stored starttime values fall exactly on local midnight, and so whether any day is actually skipped, depends on CRM data and runtime culture that are not in the files. The text must be conditional, for example: 'יום נחשב לא-יום-עבודה רק אם ב-CalendarRule (שם Friday/Saturday/Holiday, 21 הימים האחרונים לפי GetutcDate) יש שורה ש-starttime שלה שווה בדיוק לחצות של אותו יום לפי שעון שרת ה-SSIS; אם הערכים השמורים אינם בחצות מקומית, אף יום אינו מדולג והסף הוא 3 ימים קלנדריים אחורה (לא הוכח מהקבצים)'. Plumbing note, not counted: Main sets TaskResult=Success even after the catch (lines 98-104). If the calculation throws, User::LastThreeWorkingDays keeps its value from before the task (design-time default 10/2/2017 5:29:05 PM, DTSX:42-46, which the unsupplied config may override) and step 6 runs with it. flow[1]-[3] are otherwise correct: the counting starts from yesterday, and the third counted day (D-3 when no day is skipped) is returned.
